title: api-gateway: routing, streaming proxy buffers, and OpenAI-compat surface tweaks
author: Sophia Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed increased tail latency and occasional client-visible truncation on long streaming sessions routed through the API gateway during high throughput traffic to OpenAI-compat endpoints (function calling / structured outputs). This PR makes targeted performance and behavior fixes on the gateway and the OpenAI compatibility layer to reduce queuing, avoid buffer overflow-induced partial payloads, and ensure routing policies preserve function-calling semantics. Summary of changes: 1) Routing policy tweak: introduce capacity-aware routing that prefers dedicated/low-latency backends for requests flagged with {streaming:true, function_call:required} and fallbacks for lower-priority backends. Adds a small in-memory tokenized request estimator to avoid sending oversized streaming sessions to constrained backends. 2) Streaming proxy buffers: increase default proxy write buffer from 64KB to 256KB, add dynamic buffer growth under sustained output conditions, and add backpressure signaling to upstream client sockets when KV-cache heavy sequences are detected. 3) Payload size limits: refine payload accept checks to allow larger structured output envelopes for OpenAI-compat responses (increase JSON envelope limit to 1.5MB) while enforcing a stricter per-chunk size (256KB) to keep streaming memory bounded. 4) OpenAI-compat layer: ensure function-calling metadata is preserved across routing decision boundaries, add deterministic ordering for tool-calls in multi-tool responses, and add a compatibility shim that maps Redwood structured output (typed blocks) to OpenAI-style function_call + arguments. 5) Telemetry and safety: annotate routed requests with routing_reason and backend_capacity tags, add metrics for proxy buffer usage, and add an alert when dynamic buffer growth exceeds 4x baseline. Backwards compatibility: non-OpenAI-compat traffic keeps previous behavior; changes are gated behind a feature flag (api.gateway.streaming.optimized_v2) and rolled out to regions incrementally. Testing and rollout: local integration tests, canary on perf-canary cluster, and a staged rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic. Impact: reduces tail latency on affected workloads ~18-27% in our perf-canary, eliminated observed partial-stream truncation cases during stress tests, and prevents misrouted function-calls. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for routing estimator - [x] Integration tests for streaming proxy buffer growth - [x] OpenAI-compat functional tests for function-calling/structured output - [x] Added metrics and dashboards - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan Commits summary: "introduce capacity-aware routing estimator", "increase streaming proxy buffer and dynamic growth", "openai-compat: preserve function_call metadata and add shim", "add metrics and dashboards", "test: add integration coverage and canary config". CI: initial run had a flaky e2e failure (streaming-proxy integration test) observed on 2026-02-12; fixed race by adding an explicit flush in the proxy (commit 3) and retriggered CI. All checks green on final run. Merge notes: squashed and merged after approvals; rollout will be controlled via api flag and monitored via new buffer_usage and routing_fallback_rate metrics.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you justify the 1.5MB envelope increase? Large JSON can regress memory on small backends.
Sophia Martinez: We limited per-chunk to 256KB and added the estimator to avoid sending these large envelopes to constrained backends. Also gated behind feature flag + canary rollout.
Maya Singh: Left nits on variable naming and requested a test for function_call ordering when multiple tools return outputs.
Sophia Martinez: Addressed nits, added deterministic ordering test (commit 4).
Liam O'Connor: Observability looks good; please add an alert threshold for pathological buffer growth (4x baseline) before merging.
Sophia Martinez: Added alert and dashboard panel; CI green after fix for the race.
release_notes: API Gateway: improved routing for streaming + function-calling traffic, increased streaming proxy buffer with dynamic growth, refined payload envelope limits for OpenAI-compat responses, added feature flag api.gateway.streaming.optimized_v2. Reduced tail latency and fixed partial-stream truncation for affected workloads.
notes: Rollout strategy: enable api.gateway.streaming.optimized_v2 in us-west canary (10%) for 48h, monitor buffer_usage and routing_fallback_rate; expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions.
